summary: Separated output filename from input content basename in buildForTarget(). Added validateVsFileName() helper parallel to existing validateCcFileName(). VS Code targets now write to persona.vs_file_name; Claude Code targets continue to use persona.cc_file_name (already validated). Updated log messages to report outputBasename instead of contentBasename. Deleted 24 old .md files from personas/ledger/vs-code/ and personas/standalone/vs-code/. Rebuilt all 48 personas — node scripts/build-personas.js --suite all --strict exits 0. Freshness check --check --suite all --strict also exits 0. Updated personas/docs/agents/project-manifest/file-tree.md with new .agent.md filenames for both vs-code/ directories.

comments.note: The existing validateCcFileName() had 'persona.role || persona.number' in the error message but lacked persona.slug, creating inconsistent error output for standalone personas (which use slug not role/number). Fixed in the new validateVsFileName() and also updated validateCcFileName() to include persona.slug for completeness.

The --check and --dry-run log messages previously displayed contentBasename (source template name, e.g. '1-planner.md') rather than the actual output filename (e.g. '1-planner.agent.md'). Updated to use outputBasename so logs accurately reflect what was written/checked on disk.

The STRICT mode scan for unresolved markers uses a regex over the full assembled output. A comment in the code notes this will produce false positives if a persona template body contains literal {{…}} inside a Markdown fenced-code block. No current personas hit this path, but it remains an undocumented fragility.

No old plain .md files remain. Edge-cases verified: --dry-run logs outputBasename not contentBasename; VS Code and Claude Code write to different filenames from independent YAML fields (vs_file_name vs cc_file_name); per-suite isolated builds both exit 0.

comments.note: The debt item noted by Developer is confirmed: STRICT mode {{…}} regex scan over full assembled output could produce false positives inside Markdown code fences. No current persona hits it, but worth tracking.

Tested the error path for missing vs_file_name and cc_file_name via inline Node.js eval of the validator functions. Both fire process.exit(1) with clear [ERROR] prefix and include persona.role||slug||number identification.

summary: Code review PASS. Implementation correctly separates contentBasename (input content template lookup) from outputBasename (YAML-declared output filename) for both suites × both targets. validateVsFileName() added symmetrically alongside validateCcFileName() — documented JSDoc, correct fail-fast behavior. All 24 legacy .md files deleted; 48 personas rebuilt with correct .agent.md extensions on VS Code targets. Manifest file-tree.md updated accurately. Generated output spot-checked: frontmatter correct, vs_file_name field present. No blocking issues.

comments.note: validateVsFileName() is called after full rendering (post-STRICT scan) in the 'Determine output filename' block, while validateCcFileName() is called before rendering in the context-building block. Since vs_file_name is also a template variable (interpolated in FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_VSCODE and FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_VSCODE), a missing field produces an unresolved {{vs_file_name}} marker and [WARN] before the fail-fast fires. Moving validateVsFileName() to the context block — symmetric with validateCcFileName() — would provide earlier fail-fast and prevent the unresolved marker from appearing in assembled output at all.

The [note_only-violation] error message in the CHECK path references contentBasename (e.g., '1-reviewer.md') instead of outputBasename (e.g., '6-reviewer.agent.md'). Post-WP-001 these two filenames diverge, so using outputBasename would make the error message more actionable when debugging stale check failures.

STRICT mode {{…}} regex scan over the full assembled output does not strip Markdown fenced-code blocks. Pre-existing issue already documented by Developer and confirmed by QA. No blocking risk in current persona set. Recommended mitigation: strip fenced blocks before scanning if any future persona template body contains literal {{…}} examples.
